newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador to cut M1, keep currency name July 1.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to cut M1, keep currency name July 1.

text.p: Ecuador will withdraw from the market all sucres that are not backed up by foreign reserves but has scrapped plans to rename the local currency when it introduces its "Convertibility plan" on July 1, a senior government official said Friday.

Although President Abdala Bucaram recently said the government was planning to rename the country's currency, such a change would require a constitutional amendment and has been dropped, said the official, who asked not to be named.
But the sucre symbol will be changed to Sc/ from the current S/ when convertibility is introduced on July 1, he said.

Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, who after leaving the cabinet advised Bucaram on economic policy, helped divise the convertibility plan, which will set the sucre on a fixed parity of four sucres per U.S. dollar.
Argentina also has a convertibility plan, with the peso on a par with the dollar.

The draft the Bucaram administration plans to send to Congress in the next few days says "reserves will be equal to 100 percent of the monetary base." It also says the Central Bank will withdraw excess sucres from the market.
